item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
组里5年老兵，终究走上了pip的道路

最近西雅图凄风苦雨，在一个组呆了5年，经历过升职，有过highlight，但是最近项目出了问题，休了两个星期假回来以后发现leadership开始清算了，我就因为不在场，就被扔了出去，回来后就喜提1-1总结邮件。曾经嘻嘻哈哈的领导翻脸不认人。觉得很不公平，也想过要fight back，最近整个人状态不好，很容易发脾气，对家里人很不公平，孩子还小。我一直以来很反对休fmla，因为没做错事凭什么要我take pay cut， 是爷们就该摆烂刷题跑路。但是这段时间下来，我也基本上决定放弃抵抗，还是休假吧，在职的每一秒都没有办法集中精力，有人ping我就心跳加快，根本没有办法专注刷题。上了快10年班，每个工作没有间断。4月份就开始吃药看心理医生，但是这个医生关键时刻竟然说不给开条，算是压死骆驼的一根稻草吧，有没有临时换医生的建议？目前好处是没有身份问题，打算休整一下，回来被pip或者terminate就找律师给领导写demand letter，出一口气吧。

补充内容 (2026-11-17 12:54 +08:00):
我并不在亚麻或者微软哈，我就是在一个传统行业remote，曾经WLB很好，不曾听说有PIP。。。

item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 人在巨硬，是否接VEO跳去亚麻 刚入职微软Senior岗位不到一年，近期工作压力大，最近manager说要加快进度deliver 几个
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
人在巨硬，是否接VEO跳去亚麻

刚入职微软Senior岗位不到一年，近期工作压力大，最近manager说要加快进度deliver 几个solid project，未来几个月表现很重要，将会决定我第一次绩效情况。
我其实不清楚第一次绩效会是几月，但我明显感觉到从大概8月以来整个大部门变得非常push，leader层面强调好几次在AI的帮助下目标10X tasks delivery。
前段时间amazon HR linkedin发信息是否要面试，于是面试完接到口头offer。

但Amazon是SDE II的offer属于down level，package和我现在的几乎一样，但我接VEO走人的话可以拿85k，有点想接。
工作内容比较一般是在Kindle subscription+，但Devices上个月才裁员吧，我过去也可能有hire to fire的风险。也不确定亚麻现在工作压力如何？
微软我当下做的工作更有意思点虽然在M365这个很毒的org底下。

我在微软的PERM在走PWD，但不确定明年4月PERM LMT能否重开。
Amazon还在正常PERM，在亚麻的朋友说近期也有LMT过的dp，我觉得PERM可能性应该比微软大些。
现在H1B还剩两年多一点时间挺紧的，并且没有140。

我觉得求稳的话在微软每天干8到10个小时应该能survive，因为这个sub-domain只有我和一个Junior同事在做，每个人现在都忙不过来，未来三个月好好干应该能过第一次绩效。

最近PERM又要改革，感觉办PERM好难，有时也在想拿包走人两年后用完h1b回国，但还是迷茫。
求指点🙏

item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 美国多州断电！副总统万斯回应：需要囤粮囤水吗？ 本周三清晨，一场威力巨大的冬季风暴正式登陆美国西海岸，加利福尼亚州首当其冲，遭遇了强降
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
美国多州断电！副总统万斯回应：需要囤粮囤水吗？

本周三清晨，一场威力巨大的冬季风暴正式登陆美国西海岸，加利福尼亚州首当其冲，遭遇了强降雨、狂风和暴雪的袭击。截至目前，加州已有超过5万名用户失去电力供应，多地交通陷入瘫痪。

尽管电力部门正在全力抢修，但由于阵风时速高达55英里，倒塌的树木和飞溅的碎片给维修工作带来了极大困难。

https://assets.1p3a.com/uploads/202611/18/230105dxckst5yqwgm6epe.png

Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E) 也已向北加州及湾区用户发出警告，要求居民提前为电子设备充电并准备好手电筒等应急物资。

除了加州，这场风暴的波及范围正向东部延伸。

内华达州、蒙大拿州、科罗拉多州和南达科他州均已发布天气预警。在科罗拉多州的前岭（Front Range）北部地区，受落基山脉地形影响，阵风时速可能飙升至75英里，足以刮断电线并损毁建筑物。

蒙大拿州官员已建议居民推迟非必要的出行。

https://assets.1p3a.com/uploads/202611/18/230018yug6ya5rkojwhqmm.png

气象专家指出，不稳定的天气系统预计将持续到周五，且另一场风暴可能会在接下来的周末再度来袭。

由于本周末将进入感恩节假期前的出行高峰，气象部门特别提醒民众密切关注路况信息，尤其是计划穿越山区的旅客。

洛杉矶和圣地亚哥等南加州地区也将在周四迎来一轮强降雨，低洼地区存在发生泥石流和局部洪涝的隐患。

目前，各大公用事业公司已启动应急响应机制，居民可通过 PG&E 或 SMUD 的实时在线地图监测所在区域的复电进度。

此次天气预警发布之际，美国社会近期也出现了有关全国性停电和应急物资储备的讨论。

当地时间11月16日，美国副总统JD Vance接受福克斯新闻主持人采访。

https://assets.1p3a.com/uploads/202611/18/230107uhhmbnukfrzhx1wx.png

在谈到近期美国发生的多起科技系统故障，以及英国、法国等国家建议居民储备数日食物和饮用水的问题时，媒体询问美国民众是否也应该为可能出现的突发事件做好准备。

万斯回应称，近期确实有不少朋友询问他，是否应该建造地下避难所，或者储备食物和饮用水。他对此表示：“我的答案是否定的。我们没有看到一场危机即将到来的迹象，但你必须为各种情况做好准备。”

这个回应也是针对近日有关五角大楼要求军事基地做好脱离外部电网、独立运行90天准备的报道。

万斯表示，这只是政府正常的应急准备工作，确保军方在危机真正发生时能够继续运转，并不意味着灾难即将来临。

截至11月18日，此次强风和冬季风暴预警仍在影响美国西部及北部部分地区。气象部门提醒居民关注当地最新预报，提前做好停电和道路交通受阻的准备。

➖ 传达室 ➖

item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
感觉Jensen 有点单纯啊

首先表明态度， Jensen是我非常尊敬非常崇拜的一个人。

但今天看了他的表态，感觉有点不现实。犹子要抢他的公司，打这国家安全的旗号。这个时候，Jensen再怎么表态自己是美国人，得到再多的赞，也没啥用，美国又没有啥群众路线，有没有啥底层革命，统治者不会考虑的。果然，下午英伟达董事会就发布了明确拒绝的信号。Nvidia这么大的一个肥肉，那帮人怎么可能放弃？

实际有效的手段也不多，这个美国都被那个邪教组织控制着，和平时期也出不了艺术生。为了出气，可以考虑回中国，像当年钱老一样，绝对会成为英雄类别的人物。

item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 senior eng下一步：应该坚守MLE还是靠向llm呢？ 楼主情况： 目前在某大厂搜广推部门，L5入组，入组3年一直没升，积攒了一
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
senior eng下一步：应该坚守MLE还是靠向llm呢？

楼主情况：
目前在某大厂搜广推部门，L5入组，入组3年一直没升，积攒了一些LLM应用的经验，但并无太多且扎实的MLE核心model技能。核心技能在我看来是用model解决问题。

但近期的一次reorg，我们组model相关的更少了，很多就是根据PM的想法做点东西，都是general business logic的那种。PM就总想着快，然后1/2 quarter后又换方向，所以TL也很少propose一些长期的方案，都是短平快的。我的感觉就是大家都装作很忙，表演式工作，熬到下次priority change就好。

我看周围MLE的组，慢慢有自己的评价指标：
1）是不是own一个重要的model
2）有没有一个strong的TL
3）有没有读paper来跟住热点

我们组2和3都没有，1是和research组合作的，我们就提供数据和serving的服务，所以1也很弱。manager也不想自己做1，外包>自研。
所以我的看法是我们组是个伪装成MLE组的general business logic组。

关于下一步的想法：
1. 在本组熬升职，毕竟有了3年多
pros：
1）和manager有trust
2）WLB好 （有娃）
cons：
1）好的项目reorg被分走了，我现在处于重新找project的状态
2）我们组在org里感觉偏边缘化
3）做的还是general business logic的东西，感觉skill set并没有提高
4）总结就是温水煮青蛙
1. 换到更hardcore一些的搜广推组
pros：
1）扩展skillset
cons：
1）promo要reset
2）从新build trust
1. 往LLM靠。核心的train/inference可能短期难以qualify，但大厂里有其他周边的机会，比如eval，各种LLM product的集成
pros：
1）往LLM靠，熟悉了，有经验了就在LLM方向里腾挪
cons：
1） WLB变差 （35hr变60hr的样子）
2）不确定性大，和一些hm聊，大厂做LLM产品相关的reorg很频繁，还和一些从这样的组里跳出来的朋友聊过，他觉得那里就是靠llm忽悠人来了。

我的一个核心问题：
1）需要坚守传统搜广推还是去LLM呢？
搜广推虽然也用generative的新技术，但总体上现在metrics更难move，以及serving cost很难justify。上一波搜广推的红利来自于deep learning的引入，现在generative技术似乎还没有这种效应？
2）如何判断一个MLE的组值不值得待？

想听听大家的看法，感谢！

➖ 传达室 ➖

item.title: Rainier FYI You wanted disclosure? You got it. How the Anthropic Money Network G
item.description:
Rainier
FYI

You wanted disclosure? You got it.

How the Anthropic Money Network Got Behind the Jensen Huang Pile-On

Two receipts per name: the money they took, and the words they said.

1. Kevin Roose and Casey Newton

The money: $480,000 from Tarbell for their new NPR show.

The words: Newton said Huang's resignation "feels like a proper end to the 'lol nothing matters' era." Roose said Huang "had to go."

On air, the credits thank Tarbell. On X, where 400,000 followers actually read them, it's just "with @NPR."

In October, Roose was "thrilled to be a Tarbell grantee." He said it to the funder. Not to his readers.

2. Alec Stapp, Institute for Progress (an AI policy think tank)

The money: more than $21 million from Coefficient Giving, including $10.5 million this July. His co-founder now runs Coefficient's public policy, and sits on IFP's board.

The words: four posts in two days. "Chinese spy." "Blackmail." Huang's "cover-up." And what investigators would find "once they start issuing subpoenas."

Coefficient didn't come up once.

3. Shakeel Hashim, Transformer

The money: "primarily funded by Coefficient Giving" (formerly Open Philanthropy), whose money comes from Anthropic investor Dustin Moskovitz.

The words: he demanded Huang disclose his conflicts of interest. He didn't mention his own.

His own About page promises: "In stories where we report on our funders or interview someone who works there, we will disclose the relationship."

That's a standard he apparently drops when pushing the exact regulatory agenda those funders bankroll. His rule, not mine.

4. Kelsey Piper, The Argument

The money: $1,000,000 from Open Philanthropy, June 2025.

The words: in 2019 she said Vox's Future Perfect section "probably would not take funding" straight from Open Philanthropy. This fall she wrote two big pieces on Anthropic. Neither mentions the million.

2019 Kelsey had a rule. 2025 Kelsey had a grant.

5. Sigal Samuel, Vox

The money: her earlier Anthropic pieces carried a note that her section gets money from a foundation "whose major funder was also an early investor in Anthropic."

The words: on November 14, Huang week, she wrote about Anthropic's "$1.4 trillion IPO."

The note is gone.

6. Zvi Mowshowitz

The money: a $200,000 "unconditional gift" from Jaan Tallinn, who led Anthropic's first funding round.

The words: anyone who thinks Effective Altruism and Anthropic took Huang down has "Anthropic Derangement Syndrome."

Calling it paranoia while cashing the check. There's a syndrome for that too.

7. The newsrooms

Tarbell pays $75,000 to $135,000 to place AI reporters inside newsrooms.

NBC, Fortune, CNBC, The Verge and The Guardian all ran stories this month by reporters it pays, current or former. None said so in the stories.

NBC added a note only after OpenAI complained. Fortune put a line on an author page, because that's all Tarbell's own rule requires: the one page nobody clicks.

The Dispatch put it right with the story. See? It's not hard.

Where Tarbell's money comes from: $23,100,930 from Coefficient to date. More from Jaan Tallinn's fund. And a speaker for its fellows: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic.

8. The rest of the chorus

Rob Wiblin, 80,000 Hours ($7.7 million from Coefficient):
"His mistress's firm ended up with ~$5b worth… WITAF is this."

Miles Brundage, AVERI ($5 million from Coefficient):
"Everyone paying attention knew that NVIDIA captured Commerce long ago."

Peter Wildeford, co-founder and board member of IAPS (an AI policy institute; $34 million from Coefficient):
"NVIDIA as a whole has been nothing but ruthless and dishonorable."

item.content:encoded:
Rainier
FYI

You wanted disclosure? You got it.

How the Anthropic Money Network Got Behind the Jensen Huang Pile-On

Two receipts per name: the money they took, and the words they said.

1. Kevin Roose and Casey Newton

The money: $480,000 from Tarbell for their new NPR show.

The words: Newton said Huang's resignation "feels like a proper end to the 'lol nothing matters' era." Roose said Huang "had to go."

On air, the credits thank Tarbell. On X, where 400,000 followers actually read them, it's just "with @NPR."

In October, Roose was "thrilled to be a Tarbell grantee." He said it to the funder. Not to his readers.

2. Alec Stapp, Institute for Progress (an AI policy think tank)

The money: more than $21 million from Coefficient Giving, including $10.5 million this July. His co-founder now runs Coefficient's public policy, and sits on IFP's board.

The words: four posts in two days. "Chinese spy." "Blackmail." Huang's "cover-up." And what investigators would find "once they start issuing subpoenas."

Coefficient didn't come up once.

3. Shakeel Hashim, Transformer

The money: "primarily funded by Coefficient Giving" (formerly Open Philanthropy), whose money comes from Anthropic investor Dustin Moskovitz.

The words: he demanded Huang disclose his conflicts of interest. He didn't mention his own.

His own About page promises: "In stories where we report on our funders or interview someone who works there, we will disclose the relationship."

That's a standard he apparently drops when pushing the exact regulatory agenda those funders bankroll. His rule, not mine.

4. Kelsey Piper, The Argument

The money: $1,000,000 from Open Philanthropy, June 2025.

The words: in 2019 she said Vox's Future Perfect section "probably would not take funding" straight from Open Philanthropy. This fall she wrote two big pieces on Anthropic. Neither mentions the million.

2019 Kelsey had a rule. 2025 Kelsey had a grant.

5. Sigal Samuel, Vox

The money: her earlier Anthropic pieces carried a note that her section gets money from a foundation "whose major funder was also an early investor in Anthropic."

The words: on November 14, Huang week, she wrote about Anthropic's "$1.4 trillion IPO."

The note is gone.

6. Zvi Mowshowitz

The money: a $200,000 "unconditional gift" from Jaan Tallinn, who led Anthropic's first funding round.

The words: anyone who thinks Effective Altruism and Anthropic took Huang down has "Anthropic Derangement Syndrome."

Calling it paranoia while cashing the check. There's a syndrome for that too.

7. The newsrooms

Tarbell pays $75,000 to $135,000 to place AI reporters inside newsrooms.

NBC, Fortune, CNBC, The Verge and The Guardian all ran stories this month by reporters it pays, current or former. None said so in the stories.

NBC added a note only after OpenAI complained. Fortune put a line on an author page, because that's all Tarbell's own rule requires: the one page nobody clicks.

The Dispatch put it right with the story. See? It's not hard.

Where Tarbell's money comes from: $23,100,930 from Coefficient to date. More from Jaan Tallinn's fund. And a speaker for its fellows: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic.

8. The rest of the chorus

Rob Wiblin, 80,000 Hours ($7.7 million from Coefficient):
"His mistress's firm ended up with ~$5b worth… WITAF is this."

Miles Brundage, AVERI ($5 million from Coefficient):
"Everyone paying attention knew that NVIDIA captured Commerce long ago."

"NVIDIA as a whole has been nothing but ruthless and dishonorable."
